name: audio-meters

frames.best_why: Master meter is near full with red segments lit, the red clip count shows and the channel bars peak.

tagline: Broadcast-style LED level meters that bounce with the beat and flag clipping.
summary: A two-channel master LED meter with a dB scale, a live readout and a clip light, above six vertical gradient meters for Kick, Snare, Bass, Keys, Vocal and FX that move with synthetic audio.
appearance: A dark panel titled Master bus holds two stacked rows of tiny square LED segments shifting from green through yellow to red, with a dB scale underneath. Below, six thin vertical bars in matching colours rise from the floor, each with a tiny peak tick.
behaviour: Every bar jumps and settles with the beat, leaving a small peak-hold marker at its high point. The readout counts the level in decibels, and when a channel pushes past zero the segment row and a red clip light come on.
demo_content: A master bus at 112 BPM plus six stems: Kick, Snare, Bass, Keys, Vocal and FX.
search_phrases: audio level meter with led segments
vertical channel meters in a mixer
use_when: An audio tool or player needs a realistic level display with channels, a decibel scale and clipping.
avoid_when: It needs a frame source and real dB values, so on its own it renders flat silent tracks.
customise: Compose tracks from Channel, Track, Bar and Hold parts and pass a source, or declarative peakDb, rmsDb or channels. Range, zones, ballistics, taper, size and variant are props.
weight_why: A per-frame painter writes CSS variables while levels move, then sleeps when settled or hidden.

a11y.note: It uses role meter with live aria-valuenow and valuetext, and switches to instant, throttled updates under reduced motion.

issues: The dB scale labels and clip counts are tiny grey text, hard to read.
The demo drives synthetic levels, so values do not correspond to real audio.
polish_why: Convincing broadcast meter with peak hold and clip light; the scale and counts are very small.
